parameters.content:
# Chat Entry Point

Starts when a user sends a message through n8n Chat.

Examples:
- Summarize unread emails
- Draft a reply
- Find calendar availability
- Book a meeting after approval

# Supervisor AI Agent

Routes user requests to the Inbox or Calendar specialist.

The Supervisor must ask for explicit approval before instructing tools to send email or change calendar events.

# Ollama Configuration

Configured credential: Ollama iMAC Mini 192.168.1.10.

Confirm the base URL and model are reachable from the n8n container before activating a new import.

# Gmail Configuration

Configured credential: Gmail account.

Required safety test:
- Read email
- Create draft
- Send only after explicit approval command

# ACTION TOOLS HARD-DISCONNECTED

The following Gmail/Calendar mutation tools remain on the canvas but are not connected as AI tools:
- Draft_Email
- Send_Email
- Book_Meeting
- Update_Meeting
- Cancel_Meeting

This is an enforced graph-level safety gate, not just a prompt rule. The assistant may read Gmail and Calendar, summarize, and propose exact changes, but it cannot mutate Gmail or Calendar from the AI agent path.

Only reconnect these through a native approval executor that applies a stored, exact action after the user approves through Telegram or WhatsApp.

# Google Calendar Configuration

Configured credential: Google Calendar account.

Required safety test:
- Check availability first
- Book/update/cancel only after explicit approval command

# Workflow Overview

Safe personal productivity assistant.

The graph contains read-only Gmail and Calendar tools plus hard-disconnected mutation placeholders.

Session memory is partitioned by agent role:
- supervisor
- inbox
- calendar

This prevents one specialist's local thread state from bleeding into another specialist's memory window.

parameters.toolDescription: DISCONNECTED SAFETY PLACEHOLDER. Updates calendar events only from a native approval executor after Telegram/WhatsApp approval of exact event ID and changes.

parameters.content:
# Approval / Editing Protocol

For any Gmail or Calendar mutation, the assistant must respond with:

APPROVAL_REQUIRED
Action: ...
Exact details: ...
Approve with /approve only after reviewing.
Reject with /reject.

Supported edit commands before approval:
- /to, /cc, /bcc, /subject, /body
- /title, /time, /location, /notes, /attendees

The graph currently sends Telegram-triggered approval/proposal text back to Telegram and does not execute Gmail/Calendar mutations.

# REQUIRED BEFORE PRODUCTION

Complete these items before activating this workflow:

## n8n production checklist
- Set up error notifications or an error workflow.
- Configure time saved tracking if you want reporting.
- Enable MCP access only if this workflow must be exposed to MCP clients.

## Credentials and models
- Configure all red credential notes on this canvas.
- Confirm Gmail, Calendar, Telegram, WhatsApp/GreenAPI, and Ollama permissions before activation.

## Safety review
- Gmail/Calendar mutation tools are hard-disconnected from AI agents.
- Read-only Gmail and Calendar tools remain connected.
- Telegram-triggered mutation requests receive approval/proposal text, but no Gmail/Calendar mutation is executed by this graph.
- Add a native approval executor before enabling real write actions.

# Messaging Entry Points

This production candidate accepts commands from four sources and normalizes them before the Supervisor:

- n8n chat trigger
- Telegram webhook: /webhook/personal-productivity/telegram
- GREEN-API webhook: /webhook/personal-productivity/greenapi
- WhatsApp Cloud webhook: /webhook/personal-productivity/whatsapp

Recommended security:
- Set TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN and pass it to Telegram setWebhook as secret_token.
- Set GREENAPI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN and pass it to GREEN-API as webhookUrlToken using Bearer <token>.
- Set WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN and use the same token in Meta webhook verification.

The normalizer ignores GREEN-API non-message status events and WhatsApp status-only events.

# Native Approval Executor Required

This workflow now blocks all Gmail/Calendar mutation tools from AI-agent access.

To enable real approved writes later, add a separate native executor that:
1. Stores an exact pending action payload.
2. Sends approval buttons/commands through Telegram or WhatsApp.
3. On /approve, validates action id, user, and expiry.
4. Executes the matching Gmail or Calendar node with the stored payload.

Do not reconnect mutation tools directly to the AI agent.
